claim: Every folder a harness session starts in carries the tier hook; before a session is started in a folder, check that the hook is present there and install it if it is not.
when: before starting a session in any folder
quote: If this hook will not work in another folder, then that folder should have another hook of its own. And before starting, we should check if this hook is present there or not.

claim: tools/ensure-tier-hook.sh <folder> says whether the tier hook is wired in that folder and installs it when the folder is inside this repository and has no settings file; it will not install into a folder outside this repository without --force, because other sessions there (the product's) follow other routes and would have their helpers refused.

Two orchestrator sessions on Opus are collecting the literature on bottlenecks (o1: detecting the bottleneck and switching method; o2: scheduling under several scarce resources), and one helper reads our own logs for which resource limited which past job. Reports go to docs/program/evidence/bottleneck-2026-11-18/, records to library/journal/<date>/o1.jsonl and o2.jsonl. The top session commits their files, decides proposed corrections and writes the table from bottleneck to method.

Over 25 recorded episodes of our own work the limit changed from job to job: the serial queue in 8, blocked program starts in 6, memory in 4, the token allowance in 4, the processor in 3 (the model run with 16 workers: 88 to 91 % on average, peaking at 100 %), nothing in 1; five episodes had two limits at once. The processor share of a single job, the memory peak of a model run and the tokens of any run were never measured.

Recall test 2 of the library at version 1 (a Sonnet reader that knew nothing, 9 questions): 5 answered surely, 3 partly, 1 rightly 'not recorded'; 23 records read in 24 searches. What still got in the way was content, not format: three situations missing from the look-up table (added since), thin evidence behind some records, and one count that disagreed with the evidence summary (the summary was wrong and is corrected). The format is judged ready to fill.

Fill the library: one Haiku extractor per evidence file writes records into its own journal file, five at a time; a Sonnet reader then checks every record against the place it cites and reports duplicates and contradictions; the top session rebuilds the board. Records written from memory proved wrong five times in version 0, so nothing is written from memory.

Wave 1 of the bottleneck literature is collected and saved: ten collector files by Sonnet helpers under two Opus orchestrators (o1: detection and switching, five files; o2: scheduling under several scarce resources, five files, 47 papers, of which 14 more could not be opened by a public route). Nothing in them is analysed or refuted yet: they are collectors' readings with their marks.

The orchestrator o2 reached 132,000 tokens of context after one wave of five collectors and stopped as briefed, leaving its state and two ready briefs; the app then refused the top session's start of a fresh orchestrator on a turn begun by a session notice, so the top session ran o2's prepared analyse and refute briefs as Opus helpers itself.

Untested decision rule by bottleneck: at every start and finish of a unit of work, work out for each resource how many units it can carry now (memory: the peaks that fit in free memory above a reserve, a hard cap; processor: expected busy threads at most 24; the check: from its share of time or from its slots; shared files: conflict counts; tokens: what fits the allowance at the planned pace; and the units ready) and run at the smallest of these; the resource that gives the smallest is the bottleneck, so scheduling follows a moving bottleneck without any switch; act only at the gate, and stop running work only when memory reaches its floor.
when: Before deciding how many helpers, sessions or heavy commands to run at once, or what to do when a job is slow.
note: The minimum of the widths is argued in one paper for two limits; no program it tested had both. No number in the rule is set: each must be computed from measurements here (r57-0511).

claim: Untested: how several writers share one file is the one real switch in the rule, decided per file: places known beforehand to conflict (7 ordered sequences and 4 places where the same statements change, of our 20 shared places) get one owner at a time or are split first into separate entries, and the 9 separate entries get own copies merged later; while work runs, a file moves to one owner when the chance of a conflict times the cost of redoing a unit exceeds the cost of waiting for the owner, with cost counted in whatever is scarce now (tokens and check time for redoing, clock time for waiting), and moves back only after a set number of quiet units and only between units; every merge passes the check.
when: Before letting two helpers or sessions change the same file, and before choosing between waiting and redoing.
note: This makes the single workflow of r57-0401 one case of a rule: the case in which tokens are scarce. The threshold is not computed yet; it needs conflict counts and the cost of a redone unit (r57-0511).

claim: Untested: the next unit to start is the one whose needs best fit what is free on all resources at once, short check jobs go first, a unit queued for the check holds nothing else, and the cheaper model does a unit only where its quality gap on that kind of work was measured small; the token allowance enters the rule as one more width, which no paper covers, so that part is reasoning alone.

Measurements the decision rule needs before any number in it can be set, each needing the owner's word: per class of unit the peak private memory and busy threads over time; the time a unit spends outside the check, per piece and per change; whether one suite run slows when a second runs beside it; the suite with its test files side by side; conflict counts from a merge of dummy edits on our own neighbouring lines; tokens per unit by class and model, whether the 5-hour window is fixed or rolling, and how cached reads count; a memory-bandwidth counter only if the first three show an unexplained slowdown. The lane's wait with one slot against two needs no run: the log holds both periods.
evidence: docs/program/evidence/bottleneck-2026-11-18/DECISION-RULE.md#Numbers to compute here, and the measurement each one needs

claim: The decision rule from bottleneck to method is docs/program/evidence/bottleneck-2026-11-18/DECISION-RULE.md: a hypothesis, nothing run. Behind it are o1-report.md (finding the bottleneck and switching; 32 papers; 8 claims, all narrowed by a refuter, none refuted) and o2-report.md (scheduling under several scarce resources; 47 papers; 4 claims confirmed, 4 narrowed), their claims and refute files in the same folder, and the records o1-* and o2-*. The page also replaces the single workflow of E:several-writers-options.md with a rule per file.

Untested decision rule by bottleneck: at every start and finish of a unit of work, work out for each resource how many units it can carry now (memory: the peaks that fit in free memory above a reserve, a hard cap; processor: expected busy threads at most 24; the check: from its share of time or from its slots; shared files: conflict counts; tokens: the units the current window can still pay for above a reserve; and the units ready) and run at the smallest of these; the resource that gives the smallest is the bottleneck, so scheduling follows a moving bottleneck without any switch; act only at the gate, and stop running work only when memory reaches its floor. The token allowance is a budget and not a rate: units side by side cost the same tokens in total as one after another, so it limits how many run at once only when a window is nearly spent, and otherwise decides how many units can be done before the reset and on which model; side-by-side work costs extra tokens only through redone work and a waiting session re-reading its context.
when: Before deciding how many helpers, sessions or heavy commands to run at once, or what to do when a job is slow.
note: Replaces r57-0405, which said tokens fit the allowance 'at the planned pace': that mixed a rate into a budget. The minimum of the widths is argued in one paper for two limits; no program it tested had both. No number in the rule is set: each must be computed from measurements here (r57-0511).
